title: Mire
summary: MIRE, noun Deep mud; earth so wet and soft as to yield to the feet and to wheels. MIRE, verb transitive To plunge and fix in mire; to set or stall in mud. We say, a horse, an ox or a carriage is mired

inlines.v: MIRE, noun Deep mud; earth so wet and soft as to yield to the feet and to wheels. MIRE, verb transitive To plunge and fix in mire; to set or stall in mud. We say, a horse, an ox or a carriage is mired, when it has sunk deep into mud and its progress is stopped. 1. To soil or daub with mud or foul matter. MIRE, verb intransitive To sink in mud, or to sink so deep as to be unable to move forward. MIRE, noun An ant. [See Pismire.]
